audit_findings.title: Regulatory-cost deferrals may inflate owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $721.416M FY2025 regulatory assets; $537.355M net of regulatory liabilities; FY2025 net balance increased $63.921M, equal to 25.7% of the $248.6M OE anchor (computed)
audit_findings.mechanism: Unfunded increases in regulatory assets are additional working-capital or long-term funding requirements that reduce owner earnings; disallowed balances would also reduce earnings or the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The creation of a regulatory asset allows for the deferral of costs, which, absent a mechanism to recover such costs from customers in rates approved by the BPU, would be charged to expense on its income statement in the period incurred.
audit_findings.explanation: The large FY2025 net regulatory-balance increase establishes material scale, but it does not by itself demonstrate an OE error because the supplied OE reconciliation does not show whether the funding was deducted and some balances earn carrying returns or are recoverable from customers. The subsequent net balance decrease through June 2026 also shows that annual movements can reverse. An uncaptured recurring burden near the FY2025 amount would materially overstate the anchor and all scenarios.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 and the nine months through June 2026 account-by-account cash additions, customer recoveries, carrying income, regulatory liabilities and disallowances; then rerun OE and all scenarios using only the normalized uncompensated funding requirement.

audit_findings.title: Recurring removal cash outflows may be omitted
audit_findings.magnitude: $46.030M FY2025 outflow; $44.990M three-year average (computed), equal to 18.1% of the $248.6M anchor; the related regulatory asset increased only $2.010M in FY2025
audit_findings.mechanism: Removal spending is a recurring maintenance-related cash outflow outside current-period property expense and must enter the OE reinvestment deduction, net of customer-funded accruals, recoveries and related regulatory-balance movements.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon retirement, the cost of depreciable property, plus removal costs less salvage, is charged to accumulated depreciation with no gain or loss recorded.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring cash outflow is demonstrated, while its omission from OE is not demonstrated because no maintenance-reinvestment reconciliation was supplied. The small $2.010M increase in the related regulatory asset indicates substantial accounting or customer-funding offsets, but it does not prove that the OE calculation captured them correctly. Gross omission at the filed three-year run rate would materially overstate OE.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $46.030M FY2025 removal payment and the three-year history through accumulated depreciation, expense, customer collections and the cost-of-removal regulatory account; rerun OE with the normalized net cash burden exactly once.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 anchor may retain the divestiture gain
audit_findings.magnitude: $58.2M pre-tax consolidated gain, equal to 23.4% of the $248.6M OE anchor; transaction-specific after-tax amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any retained after-tax sale gain raises the FY2025 OE anchor and is then propagated through every forecast year and terminal value despite originating from disposed assets.
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal 2025, the Company recognized a pre-tax gain on sale of assets of approximately $ 58.2 M on the Consolidated Statements of Operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The nonrecurring gain and its material size are demonstrated. Inclusion in OE remains unresolved: the cash-flow statement removes the gain when reconciling operating cash flow, but the supplied valuation does not provide an OE bridge proving that the entire after-tax gain was removed. The perimeter note alone does not cure a retained numerator adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Produce the FY2025 OE bridge from reported net income and identify the full consolidated tax effect of the $58.2M gain, including the $56.187M CEV component; if any amount remains, remove it and rerun the anchor and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Equity-method earnings may lack the corresponding reinvestment burden
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.813M FY2025 S&T equity earnings explicitly reported; $6.067M consolidated equity-in-earnings line; distributions exceeded equity earnings by $0.612M; unreported pro-rata maintenance burden unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: OE includes affiliate earnings, but consolidated capital expenditures exclude the affiliate's maintenance investment and retained senior cash needs; sustainable distributions should replace accounting earnings unless pro-rata reinvestment is deducted.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company holds a 50 % equity method investment in Steckman Ridge, a jointly owned and controlled natural gas storage facility located in Bedford County, Pennsylvania.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting mismatch is possible but not demonstrated. FY2025 distributions exceeding equity earnings argues against a current cash shortfall, and the explicitly reported S&T equity earnings were only 1.5% of the anchor. The record does not disclose Steckman Ridge's maintenance capital, debt service, reserves or sustainable distributions, so it cannot establish whether the longer-term adjustment is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain Steckman Ridge's FY2023-FY2026 cash-flow statements, capital expenditures, debt service, partner contributions and distributions; replace equity earnings with normalized distributable cash or deduct NJR's pro-rata maintenance burden and rerun if the difference is material.

audit_findings.title: Finite AMA income may have been capitalized as perpetual
audit_findings.magnitude: $19.7M FY2025 AMA revenue, equal to 7.9% of the $248.6M anchor; $34M annual cash receipts through FY2031; $56.4M deferred revenue at June 30, 2026; net OE contribution unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: AMA revenue and its net cash contribution enter OE only through the contract period; carrying the FY2025 contribution into terminal earnings overstates forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: NJR received a total of approximately $260M in cash from fiscal 2022 through fiscal 2024 and will receive approximately $34M per year from fiscal 2025 through fiscal 2031 under the agreements.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual end date and finite revenue are demonstrated. Capitalization as a perpetuity remains unresolved because the supplied valuation describes a general growth-and-fade forecast but no explicit AMA runoff or OE bridge. Since the agreements end by FY2031, before the model reaches terminal earnings, any retained contribution could materially distort the roughly 48%-52% terminal-value component.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile AMA cash receipts, recognized and deferred revenue, demand-fee obligations and taxes by year through FY2031; forecast the resulting net OE contribution to zero by contract expiry and rerun every scenario and terminal value.

audit_findings.title: Underfunded retiree benefits are a senior economic claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $98.221M FY2025 OPEB deficit; $69.089M combined pension-and-OPEB net deficit (computed), equal to 2.0% of $3.527B base equity value and $0.67 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: The nonrecoverable unfunded portion is a claim ahead of common equity in the bridge; recurring cash contributions exceeding benefit expense would also reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In these circumstances, we may be required to recognize increased pension and OPEB expenses and/or be required to make additional cash contributions into the plans.
audit_findings.explanation: The underfunding is demonstrated, but the filed scale is not large enough to change the valuation conclusion. Deducting the entire computed $69.089M combined deficit would reduce base value from $34.45 to about $33.78 per share, still far below the $53.40 price. The actual shareholder claim should be smaller to the extent NJNG's portion is recoverable through regulatory assets; expected OPEB contributions of up to $3.0M annually are also only 1.2% of the OE anchor.
audit_findings.action: Allocate the funded deficit and future contributions between regulated-recoverable and unregulated operations, confirm that contribution expense is not double-counted in OE, and deduct only the nonrecoverable net amount in the bridge.
